title: MajorTOM Burst
description: ELLIOT-Pretrain is a multi-modal Earth Observation dataset for fast pre-training of AI foundation models, built on the Major TOM global 10 km grid. It provides co-registered 10.56 km tiles with Sentinel-2, Landsat 8/9, Sentinel-1 RTC, Copernicus DEM, ESA WorldCover, cloud masks, ERA5 weather and OpenStreetMap features in three temporal regimes: monotemporal, monthly, and burst. This burst sub-dataset covers 16,666 tiles with 6 timesteps at ~5-day cadence for rapid events.

providers.name: Image and Signal Processing Group (ISP), Universitat de Valencia

readme: ## README.md # Major TOM ELLIOT-Pretrain [![Source Cooperative](https://img.shields.io/badge/Source_Cooperative-elliot--pretrain-blue)](https://source.coop/major-tom/elliot-pretrain) [![TACO v3](https://img.shields.io/badge/format-TACO_v3-green)](https://github.com/asterisk-labs/taco/blob/main/spec/main.md) [![Open In Colab](https://colab.research.google.com/assets/colab-badge.svg)](https://colab.research.google.com/github/elliot-project/majortom-elliot-tasks/blob/main/examples/release/example.ipynb) [![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-CC--BY--SA--4.0%20%2B%20ODbL--1.0-orange)](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/) ELLIOT-Pretrain is a Major TOM expansion focused on **fast pre-training** of multi-modal AI foundation models on Earth Observation data. * Built on the original [MajorTOM](https://github.com/ESA-PhiLab/Major-TOM) global 10 km grid * 10.56 km tiles with harmonised 10 m resolution across all sensors for fast access * Co-registered optical, thermal, radar, elevation and land cover in every tile, with a cloud mask for every optical acquisition, the weather at each acquisition, and the tile's OpenStreetMap features * Three sub-datasets covering complementary temporal regimes Tile locations were selected using hierarchical spherical k-means clustering over [AlphaEarth Foundation](https://huggingface.co/Major-TOM/AlphaEarth-Foundations) embeddings to maximise global environmental diversity. The dataset follows the [TACO v3 specification](https://github.com/asterisk-labs/taco/blob/main/spec/main.md). ## Sub-datasets | Part | Name | Tiles | Timesteps | Cadence | Purpose | |------|------|-------|-----------|---------|---------| | A | Monotemporal | 250,000 | 1 | n/a | Global coverage, spatial diversity | | B | Monthly | 12,500 | 12 | one per calendar month, from different years | Seasonal dynamics, phenology | | C | Burst | 16,666 | 6 | ~5-day (Sentinel-2) | Rapid events, floods, fires, landslides | All three parts share the same layers. | Layer | Source | Resolution | Content | |----------|--------|------------|-------| | Sentinel-2 L1C | ESA Copernicus | 10 m | 13 spectral bands | | Landsat 8/9 OLI-TIRS | USGS | 30 m | 11 bands (9 OLI + 2 TIRS) | | Copernicus DEM GLO-30 | ESA / TanDEM-X | 30 m | elevation | | ESA WorldCover | ESA | 10 m | land cover class | | Sentinel-1 RTC | Catalyst, via Microsoft Planetary Computer | 10 m | VV, VH (linear gamma-0), one image per Sentinel-2 frame, acquired as close to it as possible | | Cloud and shadow masks | OmniCloudMask | 10 m | one per Sentinel-2 and Landsat frame: 0 clear, 1 thick cloud, 2 thin cloud, 3 shadow | | ERA5 | Copernicus Climate Change Service | — | 2 m temperature and dewpoint, humidity, precipitation, cloud cover and 10 m wind at each acquisition | | OpenStreetMap | © OpenStreetMap contributors | vector | the tile's features and administrative units, as GeoParquet | Each tile also carries its WorldCover histogram, DEM statistics, cloud summaries and its climate, soil, socioeconomic and administrative context. ## Quick Start Pick a tile index from Part A (monotemporal) and visualize its layers. ```python import numpy as np import rasterio import matplotlib.pyplot as plt BASE = "https://data.source.coop/major-tom/elliot-pretrain" IDX = 42 # change this to explore different tiles MODS = ["s2", "l8", "s1", "dem", "lc"] fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 5, figsize=(25, 5)) for j, mod in enumerate(MODS): url = f"/vsicurl/{BASE}/monotemporal/DATA/{IDX}/{mod}/data.tif" with rasterio.open(url) as src: if mod in ("s2", "l8"): rgb = src.read([4, 3, 2]).astype(np.float32) axes[j].imshow(np.clip(rgb / 3000, 0, 1).transpose(1, 2, 0)) elif mod == "s1": vv = src.read(1) axes[j].imshow(10 * np.log10(np.where(vv > 0, vv, np.nan)), cmap="gray", vmin=-25, vmax=0) elif mod == "dem": axes[j].imshow(src.read(1), cmap="terrain") else: axes[j].imshow(src.read(1), cmap="tab20") axes[j].set_title(mod) axes[j].axis("off") plt.tight_layout() plt.show() ``` ## Notebooks * [`example.ipynb`](https://data.source.coop/major-tom/elliot-pretrain/example.ipynb) ([open in Colab](https://colab.research.google.com/github/elliot-project/majortom-elliot-tasks/blob/main/examples/release/example.ipynb)): all three parts with general-purpose libraries (`pandas`, `rasterio`, `geopandas`): metadata queries with filtering, every layer, and a streaming PyTorch DataLoader with parallel fetching. * [`example_taco.ipynb`](https://data.source.coop/major-tom/elliot-pretrain/example_taco.ipynb) ([open in Colab](https://colab.research.google.com/github/elliot-project/majortom-elliot-tasks/blob/main/examples/release/example_taco.ipynb)): the same data through the [TACO](https://github.com/OscarPellicer/taco) reader, which decodes every layer of a tile in one call from the dataset's own contract (bands, units, scaling, frame times). For vision-language tasks built from these layers (captions, grounding, grids, phenology and change questions, with scorers and a PyTorch loader), see [majortom-elliot-tasks](https://github.com/elliot-project/majortom-elliot-tasks). ## Dataset Structure ``` elliot-pretrain/ ├── monotemporal/ # Part A, 250k tiles, 1 timestep │ ├── COLLECTION.json # structure, column descriptions, ml:contract │ ├── METADATA/ │ │ ├── sample.parquet # one row per tile │ │ ├── children.parquet # one row per top-level entry of a tile │ │ ├── children__s2.parquet # one row per Sentinel-2 file, with ERA5 │ │ ├── children__l8.parquet # one row per Landsat file, with ERA5 │ │ ├── children__s1.parquet # one row per Sentinel-1 file │ │ ├── children__cloud_s2.parquet # one row per Sentinel-2 cloud mask │ │ ├── children__cloud_l8.parquet # one row per Landsat cloud mask │ │ ├── children__dem.parquet │ │ └── children__lc.parquet │ └── DATA/{tile_id}/ │ ├── s2/data.tif l8/data.tif s1/data.tif dem/data.tif lc/data.tif │ ├── cloud_s2/data.png cloud_l8/data.png │ ├── osm.parquet │ └── admin.parquet ├── monthly/ # Part B, 12.5k tiles, 12 timesteps │ ├── COLLECTION.json │ ├── METADATA/ # same levels │ └── DATA/{tile_id}/ │ ├── s2/img_00.tif ... img_11.tif l8/... s1/... │ ├── cloud_s2/img_00.png ... img_11.png cloud_l8/... │ ├── dem/main.tif lc/main.tif │ └── osm.parquet admin.parquet ├── burst/ # Part C, 16.7k tiles, 6 timesteps (~5-day) │ └── ... # same as monthly, img_00 ... img_05 └── facts/ # precomputed per-tile facts, see below ``` A row of a per-file table belongs to the tile whose index starts its `internal:relative_path` (`400/s2/img_03.tif` is tile 400). The tile centroid in `sample.parquet` is `ml:geometry`, WKB in EPSG:4326. `facts//facts-NNNNNN.parquet` holds, for every tile, the measured fact sheet, the series facts of a monthly or burst tile, and NDVI and land-cover grids, as written by [majortom-elliot-tasks](https://github.com/elliot-project/majortom-elliot-tasks), so its tasks and captions can be built without reading a pixel. ## Changes in this version * **Corrected metadata.** In `burst`, the per-tile columns and the per-acquisition rows were attached to the wrong tiles; monotemporal Sentinel-2 timestamps were partly in microseconds and its Sentinel-2 geotransforms were wrong; several unit descriptions were wrong. All are corrected, each correction is listed in every `COLLECTION.json` under `ml:metadata_revision`, and the pixels are unchanged. * **New layers.** Sentinel-1, cloud and shadow masks, ERA5, OpenStreetMap and per-tile statistics, added by the Image and Signal Processing Group (ISP), Universitat de València. * **TACO 0.14.** Every part is written by the TACO 0.14 writer, with an `ml:contract` declaring each layer's bands, units and scaling, and validates with it. Metadata files follow the TACO v3 level names (`sample.parquet`, `children__*.parquet`, formerly `collection.parquet` and `sample__*.parquet`). * **`wc/` removed.** `monotemporal/DATA/{tile_id}/wc/data.tif` was a byte-identical copy of `lc/data.tif` on every tile. ## Citation ```bibtex @inproceedings{francis2024majortom, title={Major TOM: Expandable Datasets for Earth Observation}, author={Francis, Alistair and Czerkawski, Mikolaj}, booktitle={IGARSS 2024}, pages={2935--2940}, year={2024}, doi={10.1109/IGARSS53475.2024.10640760} } ``` ## License CC-BY-SA-4.0, except the OpenStreetMap files (`osm.parquet`, `admin.parquet`) and `facts/`, which holds OpenStreetMap names and geometries: those are under the [Open Database License (ODbL-1.0)](https://opendatacommons.org/licenses/odbl/1-0/), © OpenStreetMap contributors. Required credits: contains modified Copernicus Sentinel data; contains modified Copernicus Climate Change Service information (ERA5); Sentinel-1 RTC by Catalyst, as published on Microsoft Planetary Computer (CC-BY-4.0); ESA WorldCover (CC-BY-4.0); Copernicus DEM; Landsat courtesy of the U.S. Geological Survey; cloud masks computed with OmniCloudMask; © OpenStreetMap contributors. ## Acknowledgements ELLIOT-Pretrain has been made possible thanks to [Asterisk Labs](https://asterisk.coop), the [ELLIOT](https://elliot-ai.eu) project (European Commission, Horizon Europe, Grant 101214398), and the [Image and Signal Processing Group (ISP)](https://isp.uv.es) at Universitat de Valencia.
